fullText:
Summary: Aitken Spence Hotel Holdings PLC (AHUN.N0000) owns resorts mostly in the Maldives, with hotels in Sri Lanka, Oman and India. The six months to September 2026 were worse than last year: a loss of Rs 4.81 a share against Rs 2.89, as the Maldives and Middle East lost Rs 2.0bn before tax (Rs 0.74bn) and finance costs rose 21%. At Rs 84.00 the share is about 0.98x its NAV of Rs 86.14 and 11.6x trailing earnings of Rs 7.24. Return on equity has never reached 12% in ten years, and debt plus leases (Rs 49.8bn net) is now 1.2x the group's equity. On this site's standard required return (20.8% for a business this geared), the hotels earn well below what shareholders should demand, so the methods value it at about Rs 41.30, about half the price. I'd buy only at up to about Rs 35 and treat under Rs 31 as a strong buy. The fall from Rs 69.50 is mostly the new, stricter required return, partly the weaker half-year.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 84.00 (CSE closing price, 2026-11-20). Please check it live. It traded between Rs 80.00 and Rs 94.80 in July–September 2026 and Rs 84.70–102.75 in April–June; it was Rs 120.50 a year earlier.
Six months to 30 September 2026 (group, unaudited): revenue Rs 20.42bn, flat. Loss from operations Rs 0.53bn (a Rs 0.39bn profit a year earlier); finance costs up 21% to Rs 2.01bn; loss attributable Rs 1.62bn, Rs 4.81 a share (Rs 0.97bn, Rs 2.89). July–September alone: revenue up 13% to Rs 11.38bn, loss Rs 1.92 a share (Rs 1.85).
Segments (half-year, before tax): South Asia and Middle East (mainly the Maldives) lost Rs 1.99bn (Rs 0.74bn); Sri Lanka lost Rs 0.16bn (Rs 0.34bn), with its resorts just profitable. Five of the six months are the off-season.
Trailing 12 months: EPS about Rs 7.24 (Rs 9.16 for 2025/26 plus this half's Rs 4.81 loss less last year's Rs 2.89).
Balance sheet (30 Sep 2026): NAV Rs 86.14 a share (Rs 88.13 in March). Borrowings Rs 40.96bn (including the new Rs 5bn debenture and Rs 6.80bn of overdrafts), leases Rs 22.35bn, cash and deposits Rs 13.50bn: net debt Rs 49.81bn, up from Rs 41.82bn in March, 1.19x group equity of Rs 42.01bn.
Cash flow (half-year): operating cash flow Rs -4.79bn, mostly money moved within the group (Rs 2.83bn repaid to Aitken Spence PLC, and Rs 2.17bn more now owed by it: Rs 4.26bn in all). Capex Rs 0.85bn, lease repayments Rs 1.26bn, interest paid Rs 1.04bn.
Debenture: Rs 5bn listed senior unsecured debentures issued in September 2026 at 12.60–13.15% for 5 and 7 years. Rs 4.2bn repays parent-group short-term loans and one bank loan (Rs 2.7bn used by September); Rs 0.8bn is for refurbishing hotels within three years.
Dividend: Rs 0.28 for 2025/26, paid in the half; no interim.

Required return
Beta 1.22: Damodaran's global hotel beta of 0.66 (unlevered, cash-corrected) relevered for net debt of 1.21x the equity's market value (market cap Rs 28.25bn plus minorities Rs 12.88bn). No local 5-year betas could be found. Cost of equity 8.24% + 1.22 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 20.8% (bear 22.3%, bull 19.3%). That is high because the group carries a lot of debt and leases for its size.

Methods (bear / base / bull, Rs a share)
NAV method, 0.5x / 0.7x / 0.9x NAV of Rs 86.14: 43.07 / 60.30 / 77.53, weighted 58.58.
P/E method, EPS to March 2027 Rs 4.70 / 6.70 / 8.70 × justified P/E of about 3.8x / 4.1x / 4.5x: 18.01 / 27.37 / 39.37, weighted 26.96. Base EPS is 27% below 2025/26's Rs 9.16 because the half-year loss is already booked; it assumes a second half of Rs 11.50 against Rs 12.06 last year.
Justified price to book, ROE 9 / 11 / 13% against the cost of equity: 29.70 / 38.71 / 50.67, weighted 38.40.
Averages: Rs 30.26 / 42.13 / 55.86.
The cash-flow DCF used last time (Rs 82.80) is dropped for now. The house method values the whole company before interest at WACC and then takes off net debt; that needs depreciation, operating profit and interest paid for 2025/26 from the annual report, which wasn't among this run's reports. A /redo AHUN full would rebuild it.
Growth check: long-run growth 2% / 3% / 4% against 11.3% supported (share of profit kept × ROE). While ROE is below the required return, growth adds little value.

Fair value and buy price
Fair value: weighting 30/50/20 gives Rs 41.31 (0.48x NAV), so Rs 84.00 is about double it.
Buy price: a 15% margin of safety gives Rs 35.12, and 25% gives Rs 30.98.
Why it fell from Rs 69.50: mainly the site's new standard required return (20.8%, from beta and debt, against the 16.5% set by hand last time), which makes the low ROE count against the share, and the DCF being set aside; partly the bigger half-year loss and Rs 8bn more net debt.
Plan for 500 shares: 200 at up to Rs 41.30, 150 at up to Rs 35.10 and 150 at up to Rs 31.00. That averages about Rs 36.35, Rs 18,175, against Rs 42,000 at Rs 84.00.
Realism: Unrealistic for now. Rs 41.30 is about half today's Rs 84.00; the lowest price in the last two quarters was Rs 80.00 and the share hasn't been near Rs 41 since before 2023 (Rs 35.50 in March 2022). Only a tourism shock or a much worse year would bring it there.

Business tests: 1 of 4 passed (weak), category 3 (avoid for now), unchanged. ROE 11.6% at best; net debt 1.19x equity; a loss in 2022/23 and growing off-season losses; cash generation passes over a full year.

Sensitivity (justified price to book, Rs a share, growth 3%)
Cost of equity 19.3%: 31.7 / 42.3 / 52.8 for ROE 9% / 11% / 13%.
Cost of equity 20.8%: 29.0 / 38.7 / 48.4.
Cost of equity 22.3%: 26.8 / 35.7 / 44.6.

What would change my view
Supports a higher value: a strong October–March season in the Maldives; ROE above 15% for more than a year; net debt falling below equity; a weaker rupee; a lower beta from Damodaran's emerging-markets data or local 5-year betas.
Supports a lower value: another loss-making year in the Maldives; finance and lease costs rising faster than revenue; a travel shock; a stronger rupee; more cash lent to the parent group.

Shareholders: Aitken Spence PLC holds 71.21% (about 74.4% with three subsidiaries) and the EPF 9.37%; the public holds 25.45% (6,382 holders).

These are my estimates from the annual reports for the years to March 2025 and March 2026 (amended version) and the interim reports to September 2026. The interim figures are unaudited, so check the price before ordering. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.
